experiment_design.technical_details: This experiment tests the hypothesis that current catastrophic weather prediction models suffer from methodological overfitting to 'decided cases' (ex-post explanation) rather than genuine ex-ante predictive capability. The study involves two phases: (1) A meta-analysis of validation protocols in top-cited disaster forecasting literature to quantify the prevalence of retrospective fitting vs. prospective validation; (2) A comparative modeling experiment where identical architectures (e.g., LSTM, Transformer-based spatiotemporal models) are trained on historical extreme weather data (hurricanes/cyclones) under two regimes: 'Ex-Post' (random temporal split allowing look-ahead bias) and 'Ex-Ante' (strict chronological split with no future data leakage). Performance will be evaluated using extreme-event specific metrics (Brier Score, AUPRC, Top-K Recall) to assess generalization stability.

Evaluate both on the same hold-out test set representing 'future' unseen events.
